Categories.value: 1936 24 Hours of Spa|Aston Martin racing cars|Images with annotations|Jim Elwes|PD Old|Template Unknown (author)|CC-PD-Mark|Maurice Falkner|William Headlam|Aston Martin Ulster LM17|Aston Martin Speed Model LM23

ImageDescription.value:
Aston Martin LM17 LM23 and 588 at 1936 Spa.
  • At right, it is an Aston Martin Speed (since exhaust pipes exit on right hand side), should be LM23 driven by owner Jim Elwes (walking,looking at middle car) and co-driver Alasdair MacRobert (darker pilot jacket).
  • In middle, looks like the Aston Martin Ulster LM17 driven by owner Maurice Falkner (fiddling with his jacket), the man behind should be his co-driver Alain Norman Latham Maclachlan.
  • Seen at left is the third Aston Martin, an Ulster (chassis 588), it won it's class (1,5 litre) driven by W. S. Headlam and W. Wood (the two left most men).[1].

ImageDescription.value:
Mini (BMW Group) on a country lane in the Börnste hamlet, Kirchspiel, Dülmen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
The vehicle was illuminated from the front and from the side.
The Mini dates back to the classic Mini from 1959, which was developed by Alec Issigonis for the British Motor Corporation. With its transversely mounted engine and front-wheel drive, it was revolutionary in terms of space efficiency and became a cult car of the 1960s.
After several changes of ownership, BMW took over the brand and launched a modern reissue in 2001. The new Mini was larger and safer, but retained the retro design with round headlights and a contrasting roof.
The modern Mini stands for compact size, a sporty “go-kart feeling”, individual design options, and modern technology—from the classic 3-door model to the electric version.
